od.title: Someone is overdosing
od.s1: Call 911. Say someone is not breathing.
od.s2: Try to wake them. Shout their name. Rub the middle of their chest hard.
od.s3: If you have Narcan, spray it into one nostril.
od.s4: If they are not breathing, give one breath every 5 seconds if you know how.
od.s5: No change after 2 to 3 minutes? Give a second dose in the other nostril.
od.s6: Lay them on their side. Stay with them until help comes.
od.review_note: Call 911 first. The Detroit Health Department approved these steps.

about.title: About this app
about.p1: This app lists free help from the City of Detroit and community groups. Info can change. If it's an emergency, call 911.
about.independent: This is an independent project. It is not from the City of Detroit, DDOT, SMART or the Health Department.
about.p2: We don't collect your name, number, or location. There are no accounts. What you tap stays on this phone.
about.sig_ok: This list is signed, and the signature checked out.
about.sig_dev: Test build: this list is signed with a test key.
about.open: The code and the list are open for anyone to check or reuse.
about.hoods: Numbers about each Detroit neighborhood have their own tab now.
about.credits_orgs: {count} sources: the websites of churches, clinics, food pantries and other groups, and a few public lists. Every listing says which one.
about.credits_foodbanks: Gleaners Community Food Bank and Forgotten Harvest, for their pantries and mobile food trucks.
about.credits_city: City of Detroit open data, for parks, streets, recreation centers, harm reduction stations and the neighborhood pages.
about.credits_census: The US Census Bureau, for streets and ZIP codes in Hamtramck, Highland Park and Dearborn.
about.credits_thanks: Thank you to the people who run these places, and to everyone who tells us when something changes.
privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.sub: What this app keeps, and what it sends
privacy.lede: This app never asks who you are. Here is everything it keeps and everything it sends.
privacy.phone_1: The list of places, so the app works without internet.
privacy.phone_2: Places you save. You can clear them any time.
privacy.phone_4: A random key made on this phone. It is never sent.
privacy.phone_5: Reports waiting for a signal. They go out when you are back online.
privacy.where: If you tap "Use my location" or type a ZIP code, it is used on this phone to sort places by distance. It is never saved or sent.
privacy.sent_h: Sent only when you tap Send
privacy.sent_1: When you report a place (for example, "closed") or add a place: which place, what kind of report, your note if you wrote one, and the time. Phone numbers and emails in notes are removed before anything is kept.
privacy.sent_2: A code for that place and that day, made from your random key, so one phone counts once. It changes every day and for every place, so no one can link your reports to each other or to you.
privacy.never: No name, phone number, email, account, ads, or tracking. We never keep your internet address.
privacy.reset: Make a new random key. Reports you send after this can't be matched to ones you sent before, even on the same day.
privacy.reset_done: Done. This phone has a new key.
privacy.reset_failed: This phone could not make a new key. Your old key is still here.
privacy.queued_note: {count} waiting to send from this phone.
privacy.queued_unreadable: Some reports saved on this phone could not be read, so we could not send them. Nothing was deleted.

report.failed: This phone could not save your report, so nothing was sent. Please try again.
report.queued: Thanks. This is saved on your phone. We'll keep trying to send it.
report.sent_place: Thanks. We can't promise when it gets fixed. If someone is hurt or in danger, call 911.

link.owner.ser_mortgage.body: State Emergency Relief can help with a mortgage, land contract, or property tax payment. There is a lifetime limit.
link.owner.ser_mortgage.label: Read about this help
link.owner.ser_repairs.title: Emergency home repairs
link.owner.ser_repairs.body: State Emergency Relief can help pay for needed home repairs, like a furnace. There are lifetime limits.
link.owner.ser_repairs.label: Read about repair help
link.owner.probate.title: House still in a late relative's name?
link.owner.probate.body: Wayne County Probate Court is where you open an estate to put a house in the heirs' names.
link.owner.probate.label: Go to the Probate Court site
link.legal.mlh.title: Free legal help, forms, and guides
link.legal.mlh.body: Michigan's free self-help website, with forms, guides, and a tool to find legal help.
link.legal.mlh.label: Go to Michigan Legal Help
link.legal.lakeshore_apply.title: Apply for free legal help
link.legal.lakeshore_apply.body: Lakeshore Legal Aid checks whether you can get a free lawyer. People with low income and seniors can get help. Apply by phone or online.
link.legal.lakeshore_apply.label: Apply with Lakeshore Legal Aid
link.legal.clean_slate.title: Clear an old conviction
link.legal.clean_slate.body: Which old convictions clear on their own, when, and the limits.
link.legal.clean_slate.label: Read about Clean Slate
link.legal.wages.title: Report unpaid wages
link.legal.wages.body: File a complaint about unpaid wages, overtime, or sick time.
link.legal.wages.label: File a wage complaint
link.id.free_state_id.title: Get a state ID with no fee
link.id.free_state_id.body: Who can get a Michigan ID for free (like people 65 and older, veterans, and people without housing) and what to bring.
link.id.free_state_id.label: See who gets a free ID
link.id.birth_certificate.title: Order a Michigan birth certificate
link.id.birth_certificate.body: Order a copy from the State by mail, online, by phone, or at a drop box. It can take 8 to 10 weeks.
link.id.birth_certificate.label: Order from the State
link.id.id_guides.title: Guides about IDs and name changes
link.id.id_guides.body: Guides about getting ID papers and changing your name.
link.id.id_guides.label: Read ID guides
link.treatment.findtreatment.title: Find a treatment place near you
link.treatment.findtreatment.body: The federal list of drug and alcohol treatment places. Each place on it is approved by the state.
link.treatment.findtreatment.label: Search FindTreatment.gov
link.treatment.michigan.title: Michigan's drug and alcohol help page
link.treatment.michigan.body: Ways to find treatment, syringe service programs, and recovery homes in Michigan.
link.treatment.michigan.label: Open Michigan's page
link.recovery.marr.title: Recovery homes certified in Michigan
link.recovery.marr.body: MARR's list of recovery homes it has certified. The homes send in their own details, so call and check before you go.
link.recovery.marr.label: See MARR's list
link.recovery.aa.title: AA meetings in Detroit and Wayne County
link.recovery.aa.body: Meeting lists and a 24-hour phone line from the Detroit and Wayne County AA office.
link.recovery.aa.label: Find AA meetings
link.recovery.na.title: NA meetings in Metro Detroit
link.recovery.na.body: Narcotics Anonymous meeting lists and a 24/7 helpline for Metro Detroit.
link.recovery.na.label: Find NA meetings
link.recovery.smart.title: SMART Recovery meetings
link.recovery.smart.body: Find SMART Recovery meetings in person or online.
link.recovery.smart.label: Find SMART meetings
link.recovery.alanon.title: Meetings for family and friends
link.recovery.alanon.body: Al-Anon and Alateen meetings for people who love someone who drinks.
link.recovery.alanon.label: Find Al-Anon meetings
link.supplies.ssp_map.title: Find a syringe service program
link.supplies.ssp_map.body: Michigan's map and list of syringe service programs. Times and places can change.
link.supplies.ssp_map.label: See the map
link.assault.free_exam.title: A free exam, no police report needed
link.assault.free_exam.body: In Michigan you can get a medical exam after sexual assault without being billed. No one can make you talk to the police to get the exam.
link.assault.free_exam.label: Read the State's page
link.assault.compensation.title: Get costs paid and track your kit
link.assault.compensation.body: Michigan can help crime victims pay medical and counseling costs. You can also track your sexual assault kit.
link.assault.compensation.label: Read the State's page
link.taxes.heating_credit.title: Home Heating Credit: due September 30
link.taxes.heating_credit.body: Michigan's Home Heating Credit helps pay heating costs. Send the form by September 30, 2026.
link.taxes.heating_credit.label: Read about the credit
link.taxes.aas_video.title: Free tax help by video
link.taxes.aas_video.body: Accounting Aid Society does tax help over Zoom on some Tuesdays and Wednesdays, through October 7, 2026.
link.taxes.aas_video.label: See the dates
link.taxes.irs_vita.title: Free tax help from IRS volunteers
link.taxes.irs_vita.body: IRS-certified volunteers do taxes for free for people who generally make $69,000 or less.
link.taxes.irs_vita.label: Read the IRS page
link.taxes.irs_free_file.title: File your taxes free online
link.taxes.irs_free_file.body: IRS Free File software is free if your adjusted gross income is $89,000 or less.
link.taxes.irs_free_file.label: Go to IRS Free File
link.benefits.mibridges.title: Apply for benefits online
link.benefits.mibridges.body: Apply online for Michigan benefits, and find community partners who can help you apply.
link.benefits.mibridges.label: Apply on MI Bridges
link.benefits.ser.title: State Emergency Relief
link.benefits.ser.body: What Michigan's State Emergency Relief can help with, and how to apply.
link.benefits.ser.label: Read about State Emergency Relief
link.benefits.mdhhs_office.title: Find your MDHHS office
link.benefits.mdhhs_office.body: Find the Wayne County MDHHS office for your ZIP code.
link.benefits.mdhhs_office.label: Find my office
link.benefits.mi_options.title: Free Medicare counseling
link.benefits.mi_options.body: Michigan's MI Options program gives free help with Medicare.
link.benefits.mi_options.label: Read about MI Options
link.benefits.insurance_help.title: Get help with health insurance
link.benefits.insurance_help.body: Find a trained helper near you who can help you sign up for health insurance.
link.benefits.insurance_help.label: Find local help
link.benefits.ssa_office.title: Find your Social Security office
link.benefits.ssa_office.body: Look up the Social Security office for your ZIP code.
link.benefits.ssa_office.label: Find my office
link.jobs_lost.uia_file.title: File for unemployment
link.jobs_lost.uia_file.body: File and manage your unemployment claim online in MiWAM, or call the State.
link.jobs_lost.uia_file.label: Go to Unemployment (UIA)
link.jobs_lost.uia_visit.title: Book an unemployment office visit
link.jobs_lost.uia_visit.body: Make an appointment at an unemployment office, up to 14 days ahead.
link.jobs_lost.uia_visit.label: Book a visit
link.jobs_lost.register_to_work.title: To keep getting unemployment
link.jobs_lost.register_to_work.body: Make a MiTalent profile and meet Michigan Works! staff at least one business day before your first certification.
link.jobs_lost.register_to_work.label: Read the rule
link.jobs_lost.mitalent.title: Michigan's job board (MiTalent)
link.jobs_lost.mitalent.body: Search for jobs and post a résumé. People on unemployment must make a profile here.
link.jobs_lost.mitalent.label: Go to MiTalent
link.jobs_lost.wages.title: Report unpaid wages
link.jobs_lost.wages.body: File a complaint about unpaid wages, overtime, or sick time.
link.jobs_lost.wages.label: File a wage complaint
link.jobs.daw_signup.title: Sign up with Detroit at Work
link.jobs.daw_signup.body: Detroit's job and training help. Sign up online or call, then meet a career coach.
link.jobs.daw_signup.label: Go to Detroit at Work
link.jobs.job_fairs.title: Detroit at Work job fairs
link.jobs.job_fairs.body: Upcoming hiring events at Detroit at Work centers.
link.jobs.job_fairs.label: See job fairs
link.jobs.mitalent.title: Michigan's job board (MiTalent)
link.jobs.mitalent.body: Search for jobs and post a résumé.
link.jobs.mitalent.label: Go to MiTalent
link.jobs.mi_works.title: Find your Michigan Works! office
link.jobs.mi_works.body: Every Michigan Works! job center in the state. Dearborn, Hamtramck and Highland Park are served by SEMCA Michigan Works!.
link.jobs.mi_works.label: Find an office
link.jobs.youth.title: Jobs and school help for ages 14 to 24
link.jobs.youth.body: Detroit at Work's programs for young Detroiters. Some take Highland Park and Hamtramck residents too.
link.jobs.youth.label: See youth programs
link.jobs.mrs.title: Job help for people with disabilities
link.jobs.mrs.body: Michigan Rehabilitation Services helps people with disabilities get ready for, find, and keep a job.
link.jobs.mrs.label: Apply to MRS
link.jobs.veterans.title: Job help for veterans
link.jobs.veterans.body: Veterans and eligible spouses are served first at Michigan Works! offices. Tell the staff you are a veteran.
link.jobs.veterans.label: Read more
link.training.daw_training.title: Training paid for by Detroit at Work
link.training.daw_training.body: Training in health care, computers, trucking, building trades, and factory work for Detroiters who qualify. Programs change, so call first.
link.training.daw_training.label: See training
link.training.youthbuild.title: YouthBuild: paid building-trades training
link.training.youthbuild.body: Paid construction training with GED help for young adults. Ages and cities differ by program; check the page.
link.training.youthbuild.label: Read about YouthBuild
link.training.trade_connect.title: A path into the Carpenters union
link.training.trade_connect.body: Job readiness, a 4-week pre-apprenticeship, then a paid 4-month apprenticeship with the Carpenters union.
link.training.trade_connect.label: Fill out the interest form
link.training.fast_track.title: Construction jobs on City projects
link.training.fast_track.body: Construction Fast Track connects Detroiters to construction jobs on City projects.
link.training.fast_track.label: Read about Fast Track
link.training.plumbers.title: Plumbers apprenticeship: applications open
link.training.plumbers.body: A paid 5-year plumbing apprenticeship. Applications close December 18, 2026, or when 200 people apply.
link.training.plumbers.label: See how to apply
link.training.older_workers.title: Paid job training for people 55 and older
link.training.older_workers.body: The Urban League's paid job training for people 55 and older with low income in Wayne or Oakland County.
link.training.older_workers.label: Read more
link.record.after_prison.title: Job help after state prison
link.record.after_prison.body: Detroit at Work's training, paid internships, and bus help for people home from state prison in the last 5 months.
link.record.after_prison.label: Read more
link.record.project_clean_slate.title: Free record clearing for Detroiters
link.record.project_clean_slate.body: Project Clean Slate gives free legal help to Detroit residents who want old convictions cleared.
link.record.project_clean_slate.label: Register with Project Clean Slate
link.record.clean_slate.title: Which old convictions clear on their own
link.record.clean_slate.body: Michigan's Clean Slate law: which convictions clear by themselves, when, and the limits.
link.record.clean_slate.label: Read about Clean Slate
link.school.daw_ged.title: Free GED classes through Detroit at Work
link.school.daw_ged.body: Free classes with the Detroit schools and others, in person or online, day or evening.
link.school.daw_ged.label: Sign up for classes
link.school.dpscd.title: Adult classes with the Detroit schools
link.school.dpscd.body: Free adult classes for the GED, a high school diploma, reading, math, and English.
link.school.dpscd.label: Sign up with DPSCD
link.school.adult_ed_map.title: Find adult classes near you
link.school.adult_ed_map.body: The State of Michigan's map of adult education classes.
link.school.adult_ed_map.label: Open the map
link.school.hse.title: GED and HiSET tests
link.school.hse.body: Michigan accepts the GED and the HiSET. The page lists the test fees and a voucher that may pay for one try per subject while funding lasts.
link.school.hse.label: See test costs
link.school.reconnect.title: Free community college at 21 and older
link.school.reconnect.body: Michigan Reconnect pays tuition at your local community college if you are 21 or older, have lived in Michigan a year, have a diploma or GED, and no college degree.
link.school.reconnect.label: Read about Reconnect
link.school.achievement.title: College money for recent graduates
link.school.achievement.body: The Michigan Achievement Scholarship, for people who finished high school or a GED in 2023 or later.
link.school.achievement.label: Read more
link.clothes.goodfellows.title: Holiday box for kids 4 to 13
link.clothes.goodfellows.body: Warm clothes, toys, and books for kids 4 to 13 in Detroit, Highland Park, Hamtramck, and some nearby cities (not Dearborn). Apply online by October 31, 2026.
link.clothes.goodfellows.label: Apply to Goodfellows
link.baby.diaper_bank.title: Diapers each month for babies under 3
link.baby.diaper_bank.body: For children under 3 in Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties. Fill out the online form each month and pick a pickup place.
link.baby.diaper_bank.label: Ask for diapers
link.phone.lifeline.title: Money off your phone bill (Lifeline)
link.phone.lifeline.body: If you get SNAP, Medicaid, SSI or similar help, or have low income, you may get money off your phone or internet bill each month. You apply through a phone company that takes Lifeline.
link.phone.lifeline.label: Learn about Lifeline
link.phone.lifeline_providers.title: Phone companies that take Lifeline
link.phone.lifeline_providers.body: The State's list of home phone and cell phone companies that take Lifeline.
link.phone.lifeline_providers.label: See the list
link.phone.library_laptops.title: Borrow a laptop or hotspot
link.phone.library_laptops.body: Detroit and Highland Park residents can borrow a laptop, Chromebook, or Wi-Fi hotspot with an adult library card.
link.phone.library_laptops.label: Borrow from the library
link.phone.tech_hubs.title: Places to use a computer in Detroit
link.phone.tech_hubs.body: Neighborhood places in Detroit where you can use a computer, get online, and get help learning.
link.phone.tech_hubs.label: See the tech hub list
link.phone.digital_skills.title: Free computer classes and a free device
link.phone.digital_skills.body: Digital Skills Detroit classes for Detroit residents. Finish 15 hours of training and you can get a free device.
link.phone.digital_skills.label: Find a class
link.phone.eii.title: Neighborhood internet: North End, Highland Park, Hamtramck
link.phone.eii.body: Community-run home internet for Detroit's North End, Highland Park, and Hamtramck.
link.phone.eii.label: Sign up for home internet
link.phone.att_access.title: Lower-cost home internet from AT&T
link.phone.att_access.body: Lower-cost AT&T home internet if you get SNAP, SSI, WIC, or school meals, or your income is low. The price and speed depend on your address.
link.phone.att_access.label: See Access from AT&T
link.childcare.cdc.title: Help paying for child care
link.childcare.cdc.body: The State helps pay for child care while you work, go to school, or get training. Apply on MI Bridges or at your MDHHS office.
link.childcare.cdc.label: Learn about child care help
link.childcare.findprek.title: Free PreK for 4-year-olds
link.childcare.findprek.body: Free state PreK (GSRP) for 4-year-olds in Wayne County. Choose your top three places and apply online, or text for help.
link.childcare.findprek.label: Apply for free PreK
link.childcare.great_start.title: Find child care and free preschool
link.childcare.great_start.body: Search for licensed child care, free PreK, and Head Start near you.
link.childcare.great_start.label: Search for child care
link.childcare.starfish.title: Starfish Head Start and Early Head Start
link.childcare.starfish.body: Free early learning for babies to preschoolers at Starfish centers, many in Detroit, for families whose income qualifies. Fill out an interest form and they will call you.
link.childcare.starfish.label: Contact Starfish
link.rides.transit_app.title: Transit app: when is my bus coming?
link.rides.transit_app.body: A free app that shows where DDOT and SMART buses are right now, and helps you plan your trip. A company called Transit makes it. We do not run it, and neither does the bus company. SMART's own website lists it as one of the apps that get SMART bus data.
link.rides.transit_app.label: Get the Transit app
link.rides.medicaid_rides.title: Free rides to the doctor with Medicaid
link.rides.medicaid_rides.body: If you have Medicaid, your health plan gives free rides to covered care. Call the ride number on your plan card; most need 2 to 3 days' notice.
link.rides.medicaid_rides.label: See ride phone numbers
link.rides.ddot_reduced.title: 50-cent DDOT bus fare
link.rides.ddot_reduced.body: Pay 50 cents a ride if you are 65 or older, have a disability, have Medicare, or are a student. Apply for a Reduced Fare ID.
link.rides.ddot_reduced.label: Get a DDOT Reduced Fare ID
link.rides.ride_to_rise.title: Free DDOT rides for Detroit students
link.rides.ride_to_rise.body: Kids in grades K to 12 who go to school in Detroit ride DDOT buses free. Show your school ID.
link.rides.ride_to_rise.label: Learn about Ride to Rise
link.rides.paratransit.title: DDOT door-to-door rides for people with disabilities
link.rides.paratransit.body: Shared door-to-door rides for people whose disability keeps them from riding the bus. Apply first; each ride is $2.50, cash only. Same-day rides are possible.
link.rides.paratransit.label: Learn about DDOT Paratransit
link.rides.smart_reduced.title: SMART bus: 50-cent fare, students free
link.rides.smart_reduced.body: Pay 50 cents a ride on SMART if you are 65 or older or have a disability. Students with a school ID ride free.
link.rides.smart_reduced.label: See SMART reduced fares
link.rides.dearborn_seniors.title: Dearborn rides for people 60 and older
link.rides.dearborn_seniors.body: Rides anywhere in Dearborn, including to the doctor, for residents 60 and older. $2 round trip; call at least 4 days ahead.
link.rides.dearborn_seniors.label: Learn about senior rides
link.pets.grace.title: Free spay and neuter for Detroit dogs
link.pets.grace.body: Free spay or neuter, shots, and a microchip for dogs that live in Detroit. No income or breed limits.
link.pets.grace.label: Get a Project GRACE voucher
link.pets.spay_van.title: Spay and neuter van from Detroit
link.pets.spay_van.body: Drop your pet at a Detroit stop at 7 am. Your pet is fixed at the clinic in Warren and comes back the next morning.
link.pets.spay_van.label: Book the van
link.dental.healthy_kids_dental.title: Medicaid dental care for kids
link.dental.healthy_kids_dental.body: Medicaid covers dental care for children and teens through Healthy Kids Dental.
link.dental.healthy_kids_dental.label: Learn about Healthy Kids Dental
tile.day: A place to be during the day
results.none_links: We don't list any places for this yet. These programs can help:
link.beds.safebeds.title: Find an open shelter bed (313SafeBeds)
link.beds.safebeds.body: A Detroit tool for finding shelter beds in Wayne, Oakland and Macomb counties. Answer three questions and it gives you phone numbers to call. The shelter decides who comes in. It is their site, not ours.
link.beds.safebeds.label: Open 313SafeBeds
about.p3: Each listing says where it came from and when someone last checked it. If nobody has checked it, we say so.
lang.changed: The app is now in English.
lang.needs_net: That language needs a connection the first time.
map.shown: Map open. The places are marked on it.
saved.cleared_say: All your saved places are gone.
loc.on_say: Using your location. The closest places are first.
loc.off_say: Not using your location. The list is for the whole city.
map.keys: Arrow keys move the map. Plus and minus zoom in and out. Press N for the next place on the map and P for the one before it, Enter to open it, Escape to go back to the map. Everything on the map is also listed below it.
map.focus_none: No places on this part of the map. Move the map, or zoom out.
map.style_standard_note: Each kind of transport in one color
map.style_subway_note: Bus and rail drawn like a subway map
map.key_frequent: Thick line: a bus at least every 15 minutes on weekdays
map.key_smart: Line with a light stripe down the middle: SMART
map.key_trunk: Wide dark line: many routes share this street
map.key_change: White pill: you can change here
map.key_end: Ring with a name: where a route ends
map.key_qline: Dark line with light ties: the QLINE. Drawn through its stations, not along the exact track
map.key_dpm: Purple loop with arrows: the People Mover, and the way it runs
map.key_bike: Thin double green line: bike lane
map.route_every: About every {minutes} minutes on weekdays, the agency says
add.e.name: Please write the name of the place.
add.e.category: Please pick one kind of help.
add.e.what: Please write what people get here.
add.e.how_known: Please pick how you know about this place.
results.head: Places
dir.title: Directions
dir.other_apps_note: These open another app. That app will see the place you picked.
dir.caveat: Directions are computed on your phone from public maps. They are not checked for safety or lighting. If a street looks wrong, use another.
dir.caveat_times: Times are estimates. Buses may come more or less often.
dir.from_hint: Type two streets that cross. This works with no signal.
dir.building: Getting the map ready… (about a second)
dir.planning: Working out the ways to get there…
dir.none: We could not find a way to walk or ride there from where you are.
dir.no_streets: The street map is not on this phone yet. Open the Map tab once while you have a signal.
dir.failed: The map could not be read.
dir.chunk_failed: Directions could not load. Open this once while you have a signal.
dir.walk_only: No bus information on this phone yet. Open the Map tab once while you have a signal.
dir.step_end_off: Then about {metres} m to the building
dir.follow_on_say: Following along. Your location stays on this phone.
dir.route_text: The line on the map is this trip: {legs}, {range}. The numbered steps below say the same thing in words.
dir.steps_keys: Press N for the next step and P for the one before.
